Good, this confirms it's the only `*AgentTest.java` in the project and the only failure.

## Summary

Created `src/test/org/apache/commons/cli2/commandline/WriteableCommandLineImplAgentTest.java` (JUnit 3.8 style, matching the project's existing tests), with 39 self-contained test methods covering `addOption`/`hasOption`/`getOption`, `addValue`/`getValues`/`getUndefaultedValues`, `addSwitch`/`getSwitch`, `addProperty`/`getProperty`/`getProperties`, `looksLikeOption`, `toString`, `getNormalised`, and unmodifiability of the returned collections.

38 tests pass. One test fails, and it shows a real bug:

- **`testAddSwitchTwiceThrowsAndDoesNotDuplicateOption`** — `WriteableCommandLineImpl.addSwitch` (src/java/org/apache/commons/cli2/commandline/WriteableCommandLineImpl.java:90-99) calls `addOption(option)` unconditionally *before* checking whether a switch is already registered. When `addSwitch` is called a second time for the same option, it mutates the `options` list (and `nameToOption`) a second time and *then* throws `IllegalStateException`. So a caller catching the documented exception is left with the option registered twice (`getOptionCount` returns 2 instead of 1), i.e. the failed call still has a side effect it shouldn't have.

I left that test as failing since it correctly demonstrates the bug rather than the intended behavior.
